title: Seam unload, khác hẳn suspend — add ExtensionRunner.unloadExtension() that drops an extension from the registry and releases exactly its own buckets and its own fallback trampolines
wave: Wave 7 (last position, after WI-8a and WI-8b). Wave 7 is 'Sở hữu của settings và seam unload thật', M–L, ~2.5 weeks, 4 PRs. The plan places WI-9 last in M2 because the resource inventory it asserts is only complete after waves 2 and 4 have given owner-ship to timers, providers and capability state.
one_line: Add a real unload path for extensions: today 'disable' only suspends (an extension keeps its module state, its per-extension registration buckets and its installed fallback trampolines), so we add ExtensionRunner.unloadExtension(path) that removes the extension from the runner's registry, disposes exactly that extension's file-write/file-delete trampolines, and drops that extension's runtime flag values — deliberately different from setSuspendedExtensions, which keeps state on purpose so resume needs no rewire.
user_visible_effect: none yet — internal. No extension-facing API is exposed; the plan explicitly forbids surfacing unloadExtension on the ExtensionAPI until it has been exercised across all 11 buckets. The user-visible consequence arrives only when a later milestone (WI-12, deferred design) wires unload to a real user gesture; at that point disabling an extension stops its background timers and stops its file-write fallback from intercepting permission-denied writes instead of merely pausing them.
effort: M — larger than it looks. The bucket teardown itself is ~20 lines; the two prerequisites (per-extension flag values, per-extension fallback disposers) are the real work, and the test matrix is 15 rows because AGENTS.md requires one row per distinct contract.
risk: A half-real unload that leaks. An extension is unloaded halfway, half its registrations survive — strictly harder to debug than today's all-or-nothing suspend, because it converts a known limitation into a false promise. Three concrete traps, in the order the plan names them: (1) the registerFlag runtime value, which no bucket assertion can see; (2) disposing the wrong fallback trampoline (or none) — the trampoline is a process-wide module array, so a leaked trampoline keeps `hasFileWriteFallback()` true even after every handler array is emptied; (3) the quietest one — a test row written in the wrong direction passes while gating nothing. Before ticking any row, ask: which mutation turns this row red? A row that cannot answer that is not a test row, however green it is.
depends_on: WI-1 (strict, BOTH halves) — do not build unload before suspend is correct, or unload inherits timer and provider leaks. Verified: managed-timers.ts:22-68 `ManagedTimers` is a flat runner-wide `Set<Timer>` with only `clear(handle)` and `clearAll()`; there is no per-extension timer ownership today, so unload cannot release an extension's timers until WI-1 adds it.

WI-1 provider half (wave 4) — the existing `unregisterProvider(name, sourceId)` at types.ts:1745 already keys by sourceId, i.e. extension path. That is the precedent the flagValues shape change should mirror.
WI-4 (wave 2) — so wave 7 has a complete inventory of resources to release.
WI-5 (wave 3 commit 1) — so the all-runner resource inventory is complete. Specifically `reset()` must already be unconditional.
blocks: WI-12 (M2 wave 8, design-only, deferred) — the plan states WI-12 cannot be designed without WI-9.
open_questions: How do CLI-supplied flag values survive the `flagValues` reshape? `runner.ts:1098 setFlagValue(name, value)` and `main.ts:2210 extensionsResult.runtime.flagValues.set(name, value)` are both extension-less writes, and `runner.ts:1094 getFlagValues()` returns a flat `Map<string, boolean|string>`. Under `Map<extensionPath, Map<flagName, value>>` there is no obvious home for a user-typed `--flag=value`. Two candidates: (a) a separate `flagValueOverrides: Map<string, boolean|string>` layer that wins at read time and is untouched by unload; (b) `setFlagValue` fans out to every declaring extension's inner map, and `getFlagValues()` flattens on read. (a) is cleaner and means a user-set value survives unloading the extension that merely supplied the *default* — which is what a user expects. A human must pick; do not invent it.

Does anything outside the CLI genuinely need `getFlagValues()` to stay flat, or can it become a flatten-over-`this.extensions` at the read boundary only? `cli/extension-flags.ts:11 ExtensionFlagSink` only needs `getFlags()` and `setFlagValue()`, so the flatten can stay inside the runner — but confirm no SDK consumer reads `runtime.flagValues` directly before changing the type.

Should `unloadExtension` return the removed `Extension` (so a caller could re-add it) or `boolean`? The plan says nothing. `boolean` is the smaller surface and matches `isExtensionActive`'s shape; returning the object invites a re-add path nobody has designed.

Is a reload (unload + load) in scope for WI-9, or strictly unload? The plan defers cache-busting and calls module cache a follow-up — but see plan_corrections: cache-busting already exists and is already per-load, so if reload IS in scope it inherits the existing mechanism for free and the follow-up disappears. If reload is NOT in scope, WI-9 is purely teardown and there is no module-graph work at all.
test_contract: The observable contract: after ExtensionRunner.unloadExtension(path) returns true, that extension contributes NOTHING to the runner — it is absent from getLoadedExtensions()/isExtensionActive, and each of the 11 registration buckets it populated is empty — while every OTHER extension keeps working, and a flag value declared by a surviving extension is still readable. If any of this regresses, a user re-disabling an extension would see phantom commands, stale tool descriptions, dead shortcuts, duplicate flags, or a file-write fallback that silently brokers their writes to a broker they just turned off. Specifically the 15 rows defend: 11 bucket rows (one contract each, per AGENTS.md); row (a) the file-write seam, whose two halves are (i) the extension's handler is no longer invoked on a permission-denied write, and (ii) hasFileWriteFallback() returns false again — half (ii) is the discriminating one and is the row that fails if unload drains the bucket but forgets the trampoline disposer; row (b) two extensions declaring the same flag name with different defaults, unload one, the readable value must be the SURVIVOR's default — not undefined, not the unloaded extension's value; this is the only row that catches the delete-the-wrong-entry bug; row (c) an onToolRegistered listener registered by extension A does not fire when extension B registers a tool after A was unloaded.

steps.instruction: Change `flagValues` on ExtensionRuntimeState (types.ts:1739) and on the ExtensionRuntime class (loader.ts:101) from `Map<string, boolean | string>` to `Map<string, Map<string, boolean | string>>`, where the outer key is the extension path. Mirror the sourceId-keyed `unregisterProvider(name, sourceId)` two lines below it (types.ts:1745) — same ownership instinct, same key. Do NOT touch the 11 buckets on `interface Extension` (types.ts:1801-1817): they are already per-extension and need no shape change.

Delete the dead `readonly flagValues = new Map<string, boolean | string>()` on ConcreteExtensionAPI (loader.ts:184). It exists only to satisfy `implements IExtensionRuntime` on line 179; nothing reads or writes it — the only `.flagValues` accesses in the whole package go through `this.runtime`. Dropping it is what makes step 1 a genuine shape change rather than two parallel maps.

Rewrite the registerFlag write (loader.ts:265) to get-or-create the inner map under `this.extension.path` before setting the default. Keep the `options.default !== undefined` guard at 264 exactly as is — a flag with no default must still not create an inner-map entry.

Rewrite getFlag (loader.ts:291-294) so the existing per-extension gate `if (!this.extension.flags.has(name)) return undefined;` stays and only the value read becomes `this.runtime.flagValues.get(this.extension.path)?.get(name)`. The gate was already per-extension; this is what stops two extensions sharing a flag name from reading each other's value.

Convert `#fileFallbackDisposers` from `Array<() => void>` to `Map<string, Array<() => void>>` keyed by `ext.path`, and update the two push sites in initialize() to append into that extension's bucket. Without this there is no way to express "that extension's disposer" — the plan requires unload to consume exactly one extension's trampolines and never the whole list.

Rewrite disposeFileFallbacks() to drain every bucket and then clear the map, so the two existing teardown paths — session shutdown (line 410) and the re-initialize guard (line 747) — behave exactly as they do today. This is a pure refactor step: run check:ts and confirm nothing downstream of the shape change breaks before adding any new behavior.

Rewrite getFlagValues() (runner.ts:1094-1096) to flatten over `this.extensions` in load order, last-writer-wins on the READ face only. This is the decision the plan pins: two extensions declaring the same flag no longer overwrite each other at the ownership face, but a read of "what is this flag" still returns ONE value and the later-declaring extension wins. Ownership stays exact; precedence becomes a read-time concern.

Migrate the remaining two writers of the old flat map: main.ts:2210 (`extensionsResult.runtime.flagValues.set(name, value)`) and main.ts:543-544. Step 7 will not typecheck without this — do not leave it to `bun check` to find. Resolve setFlagValue (runner.ts:1098) per the open_questions decision BEFORE writing row (b) of the test, because a user-supplied `--flag=value` must not silently vanish on unload.

Write `unloadExtension(extensionPath: string): boolean` immediately after setSuspendedExtensions. Order inside the body matters: capture the Extension object before splicing; remove from BOTH `this.extensions` and `#loadOrder` (deleting only from `this.extensions` is the bug — initialize() re-installs trampolines for `getLoadedExtensions()`, which is `#loadOrder ?? this.extensions`, so a re-initialize would resurrect a trampoline for an extension that no longer exists); drop it from `#suspendedExtensions`; dispose its fallback trampolines; call `this.#managedTimers.clearExtension(path)` and `this.runtime.unregisterProvider(path, path)` (both from WI-1 — if either is missing, this item is not unblocked); delete `this.runtime.flagValues.get(path)`; then clear all 11 buckets on the Extension object. Return false when the path is unknown, so a double-unload is a no-op rather than a throw.

Do NOT expose unloadExtension on ExtensionAPI. It stays a runner-level method until it has been exercised across all 11 buckets. Also: do not try the DisposableList formulation that the dsh report rejected — that turns 9 registration methods into returning effects. The per-extension buckets ARE the ownership record; only the all-runner resources were missing, and steps 1 and 5 close exactly that gap.

plan_corrections.claim: (1) 'module graph được cache bởi runtime, nên unload thật cần cache-busting' … 'coi module cache là follow-up'
plan_corrections.correction: Cache-busting is not a follow-up; it already exists and is already per-load. `loadLegacyPiModule` appends a fresh monotonically-increasing tag to the entry specifier on every import, so every load already gets a fresh module graph. There is no cache work for WI-9 to do. The plan's 'resolve bucket teardown first and treat module cache as a follow-up' sequencing advice is aimed at a problem the codebase does not have. If reload is ever in scope it inherits this mechanism for free; if it is not, WI-9 is purely teardown and the module-graph paragraph should be deleted from the plan.
